is one of the lines in Period 4 of the Los Sengas Railway Cooperation Scheme. It runs between and , and it currently has 25 stations. This line also features direct services with and an express service with seven stations which in turn features direct services with .

History

Original plans of this line originates at Wong E-Tech and terminates at Litchi Lake, with the selling point being the fact that it passes through numerous interchanges through Comic Ward, West Metropolis Archipelago, Oasis and Punctual. However, in Period 4 of the Los Sengas Railway Cooperation Scheme, only the section between Wong E-Tech and Shony Island was approved. Meanwhile, one of the stations was renamed Sandy Heights Station to compliment development.

Subsequently, the then-developer of Tripaw left Project Nazca due to historical reasons, and Nawis Railway decided to develop Old Brightland in order to restore Tripaw development, using as the only external connection at the time.

While original plans have seen this line extending to Kelper Mount through Sharpness Plains and Upper Oasis, the establishment of meant that this line is rerouted to Oasis Bay, and proposals of direct services with of Element Hub Transit are made and approved on January 24 2023.

On the same day, the westbound extension to Summer Point within Twenty-Second Continent was also approved, with the following changes:

  • Rapid Services would stop at Sandy Heights Station
  • Rapid Services would no longer stop at Wong E-Tech Station and Tenbal Island Station.
  • Express Services are also featured, which would only stop at , , , , and .

Timeline

  • 2018:
  • March 22: Phase I construction approvedBetween Wong E-Tech and Shony Island</ref>.
  • April 10: Phase I began services.
  • September 6: Phase II Construction approvedBetween Shony Island and Galileo Heights</ref>.
  • 2020:
  • February 5: Phase II began services.
  • 2022:
  • March 4: Wong E-Tech Station reconstructed due to future extension works.
  • 2023:
  • March 11: Phase III ( - ) constructions completed.

Districts Served

  • Twenty-Second Continent
  • West Metropolis Archipelago
  • Tenbal Island
  • Shony Island
  • TriPaw
  • Oasis Bay

Line Characteristics

  • The stations in the TriPaw section of this line has undergone multiple name changes, with Mount Galileo Station being renamed twice.
  • While original plans of this line only involved Miner North Station and TriPaw Station in TriPaw, due to redevelopment in Tripaw, this plan has been modified to the current stage.
  • Twenty Village Station of Nazca Railway already had reserved structure for this line upon construction.

Future Development

This line will extend to the west and enter Cityyard Shrine in Teraleros. Moreover, to complement development plans in the Twenty-Second Continent, the section between Comic Ward Station and Sandy Heights Station will also be rerouted with an extra station added in between.

title: Splended River Bridge
safeHtml:
'''Splended River Bridge''' is a bridge that spans Splended River, and is an important transport link between Flask and Yowah. The two ends connect to Sunrise Road and Splended River Boulevard respectively.

The bridge is a part of Splended River Boulevard.

History

  • Between April and June 2016: '''Splended River Bridge''' completed construction, connecting to Kong On Street as a two lane single carriageway.
  • March 18 2017: This bridge has been converetd to a two-lane dual-carriageway and is now connected to Splended River Boulevard.

Significance

  • Splended River Bridge spans Splended River and connects Grass Crack in Flask with Yowah Point in Yowah, and serves as an important transport route besides of Nazca Railway and other Co-Op Railways

Station Characteristics

  • This station is the 500th station to be built in the Los Sengas Division.
  • This station is one of the Group 2 Gateways of Nazca Railway, and is located at approximately 20 km to the southeast of Metropolis Terminal.The other three stations in the same group are , and .</ref>
  • This station is the permanent upbound terminus of .
  • This station is the first Gateway with multiple color schemes. Besides of the Lime Concrete that signifies the Season of Spring like in other Group 2 Gateways, the Pink Wool that signifies Cherry Blossoms in Spring is also added.
  • As the last Group 2 Gateway to be built, the Style, Design and Facilities of this Station has adopted various elements from , and :
  • The overall decor and the Stone Bricks at the waterfall resembles ;
  • The Bus Terminus next to the Station resembles ;
  • Besides of the fact that this Station does not feature Cross-Platform Interchange, the Station Park Outside this Station and the Platform arrangements resemble ;
  • The Shopping Street and its arrangement is similar to and .

Fun Facts

  • This page is the 3200th page of this wiki.
  • All Group 2 Gateways make use of a shape at the sides of its walls. This Station uses Lozenges.
  • According to the Nazca Railway Development Plan 2024 Edition, prior to the construction of this station, it has already been confirmed that , , and will pass through this station, with using this station as the permanent Up Direction Terminus. Moreover, the news of and serving this station is first confirmed in a Discord Exclusive Announcement on December 28 2025.https://discord.com/channels/720326673853054978/720356555744346223/1454632209536385054</ref>
  • Among all Group 2 Gateways, this Gateway is the only Station that is '''NOT''' located next to a body of water. and are both located next to a sea, whereas is located next to Lake Winter.</ref>
  • Due to the fact that there are two main Building Materials in this Station, which are Pink Wool and Light Green Concrete, Pink Wool are used at the back together with Light Gray Concrete behind the wall next to the tracks, and uses Red Concrete, Yellow Concrete and Light Blue Concrete respectively.</ref> and Pink Stained Glass appears behind the tracks of the Upper Platforms, whereas Light Green Concrete and Light Green Stained Glass appear and replace Pink Wool in the Lower Platforms. However, since this station also uses Oak Leaves behind the Glass for both floors of platforms, the wall representative design is less obviously seen.
  • The Exits in this Station are arranged in a clockwise fashion.
  • Despite being the last Group 2 Gateway to be built, this Station is the first Group 2 Gateway in which a line (, S4E11) has both directions available for boarding, as all other lines that served any Group 2 Gateway were terminating at the respective gateway(s) before S4E11.
